clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male presented with five days of acute painless progressive bilateral vision loss and recent alopecia. Initial ophthalmology exam revealed bilateral vitritis with white tufts and globular white opacities suggestive of posterior uveitis consistent with syphilis. Subsequent CSF analysis showed a VDRL titer of 1:2, elevated WBC count (33 cells/μL), and protein level (44 mg/dL), confirming neurosyphilis. The patient was also found to be HIV positive with a CD4 count of 1347 cells/μL and a viral load of 52,900 c/mL HIV RNA. MRI of the brain and orbits was normal, and other CSF infectious workup was negative. Treatment with a 14-day course of IV penicillin G was initiated.
